title: The Blue Phone
checkpoint: Phase 5 complete (School readiness) — a mixed book for 'ue', 'ph' and 'wh' (blue, phone, when)
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book that pulls three of the trickiest new spellings together: 'ue' (blue, true), 'ph' saying /f/ (phone) and 'wh' at the start of question words (when, what). Ask your child which two letters are making the /f/ sound in 'phone' — it surprises them every time.

pages.text: Nell found a phone in the grass. It was blue, and it was not hers.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee hovering over an old blue mobile phone lying in long grass, dew on the screen. Front legs behind her back like a detective. Green and blue palette.

pages.text: “When did that get there?” said Pip. “And what is it for?”
pages.illustration: Pip landed beside the phone, head tilted right over sideways to look at it. Nell shrugging mid-air. Both baffled. Close, funny, character-driven.

pages.text: Olive was sure. “That,” she said, “keeps what it sees. You look in it and it keeps it.”
pages.illustration: Olive the owl in full lecturing mode, one wing raised, standing over the phone. Her round shape and firm expression fill the frame. Pip and Nell listening in total faith.

pages.text: Nell did not think that was true. She said it was for a chat with birds far away.
pages.illustration: Nell hovering with the phone held up to where her ear would be, eyes shut, listening hard. Olive in the background, put out. One page, two opinions.

pages.text: They both had a go. Olive held it up to her foot. Nell said hi to no one at all.
pages.illustration: Two panels: Olive's foot filling a blurry phone screen; Nell talking earnestly into a completely blank screen. Both absurd, both committed.

pages.text: Then the phone made a noise, and all three of them went right up in the air.
pages.illustration: The moment of the ring: the phone lit up in the grass and all three characters caught airborne in different directions, feathers and legs everywhere. Big comic burst of movement.

pages.text: On it was a boy. He held the phone up, and he had a big grin.
pages.illustration: The phone screen shown large and clear, displaying a simple picture of a child grinning. The three of them crowded round it, small, looking in. Soft blue screen glow on their faces.

pages.text: So they left it in the grass, so he can find it. That was the true thing to do.
pages.illustration: The blue phone back in the grass exactly where it started, seen from a little distance, three small friends walking away into the evening. Quiet, warm, satisfying.
